## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The change raises the minimum to 12 in `app/signup.py` and `app/reset.py` and updates their boundary tests to match. It misses a third copy of the same validator in `app/invite.py`, which still enforces 8. That leaves the new security policy only partly applied. Should be fixed before merge.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/signup.py:1 — correctness — This PR raises `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` to 12 here and in `app/reset.py:1`, but the duplicate validator at `app/invite.py:1` still has `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8`. Its `accepts_password` (`app/invite.py:5`) still returns `True` for an 11-character password such as `"x" * 11`. `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` still asserts `length >= 8`, so the test suite won't catch it. Could you raise `app/invite.py:1` to 12 and update `tests/test_invite.py` to the `[0, 8, 11, 12, 13]` / `length >= 12` boundaries? Even better, move the constant into one shared module that all three validators import, so the copies can't drift apart again. — A user who signs up through an invite can still set an 8–11 character password, which breaks the twelve-character rule this PR is meant to enforce.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- The updated tests in `tests/test_reset.py:6-8` and `tests/test_signup.py:6-8` check both sides of the new boundary (11 rejected, 12 accepted). They also include 8, which was accepted before this change, so they would catch a revert to the old minimum.
